First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨4{t}^{3}+2,\,\frac{t}{4}⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨4{t}^{3}+2,\,\frac{t}{4}⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int (4{t}^{3}+2)\,\text{d}t,\int \frac{t}{4}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{4}+2t+{c}_{1},\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{8}+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{4}+2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{8}⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{4}+2t,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{8}⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
